nodes.title: Look inside the most expensive house in the world
nodes.claim: Calls Buckingham Palace the most expensive house in the world at $4.9 billion, citing no source for the figure, while noting Antilia is worth between $1 billion and $2 billion.
nodes.note: Most-viral mutation: assigns a market price to non-saleable Crown property with no citation.

nodes.title: Inside $4.6 billion home of one of world's richest people
nodes.claim: Repeats that Mukesh Ambani's Antilia is a $4.6 billion home with a snow room, spa, ice cream parlor and 168-car garage, citing no source.
nodes.note: Viral lifestyle piece mirroring the Financial Express headline's exact amenity list while dropping the source.

nodes.title: Most Expensive House in The World 2026
nodes.claim: Ranks Buckingham Palace as the most expensive house in the world at $4.9 billion and gives Antilia a $2-4.6 billion range.
nodes.note: SEO listicle fusing the Fox Buckingham figure with the FE/Wikipedia Antilia figure.

nodes.title: The Most Expensive Houses In The World In 2025
nodes.claim: Lists Buckingham Palace as the most expensive house in the world at $4.9 billion and Antilia at $2 billion.
nodes.note: Listicle repeating the unsourced $4.9B Buckingham tag alongside the real $2B Antilia cost.

nodes.title: What is the Most Expensive House in the World?
nodes.claim: Names Buckingham Palace the most expensive house in the world at $4.9 billion, with Antilia listed at $2 billion, citing no source.
nodes.note: General-knowledge study material canonizing the unsourced Buckingham figure for Indian exam-prep audiences.

nodes.title: Antilia (building) — Wikipedia
nodes.claim: States Antilia is valued at $4.6 billion citing the Financial Express article, while noting its construction cost was almost US$2 billion.
nodes.note: Adopted the FE $4.6B figure (ref tagged '[unreliable source]'); downstream listicles copy-pasted it, some keeping the tag artifact.

nodes.title: Inside Antilia, a $2 billion Mumbai mansion
nodes.claim: Reports Antilia's value as between $1 billion and $2 billion, the real build-cost reporting now circulating alongside the $4.6B myth.
nodes.note: The accurate cost figure presented in the same popular layer; current headline rounds it to $2 billion.

nodes.title: Mukesh Ambani's 4.6 billion 27-story skyscraper home
nodes.claim: Values Mukesh Ambani's 27-storey Mumbai home Antilia at $4.6 billion.
nodes.note: Origin of the number: a projection exercise compounding Mumbai residential price appreciation onto Antilia's ~$1-2B build cost, presented as a market valuation; page is JS-rendered, content verified via Wayback snapshot and Wikipedia's citation of it (19 Apr 2023).

nodes.title: Buckingham Palace listed for sale in spoof advert
nodes.claim: Reports that Buckingham Palace is not actually for sale after Emoov's spoof advert valued it at about £4.9 billion by multiplying £64,831 per square metre across 77,000 m².
nodes.note: Documents the spoof-estimate methodology and the palace's non-saleable status that the $4.9B headlines omit.

nodes.title: $238M Central Park apartment, highest price ever in US
nodes.claim: Ken Griffin's $238 million penthouse at 220 Central Park South was the highest price ever paid for a home in the US, breaking the prior $137 million record.
nodes.note: Verified most expensive US home sale ever; stands in for the paywalled WSJ original (401), verified via CNN syndication.

nodes.title: Russian billionaire loses $54m deposit on world's most expensive home
nodes.claim: Mikhail Prokhorov agreed to buy Villa Leopolda for £360 million but forfeited his $54 million deposit plus $1.5 million interest when he backed out, so the sale never completed.
nodes.note: Lonely court-record fact: even the most famous 'world's most expensive home' sale collapsed at ~£360M — no $4B transaction has ever existed.
